answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a non-transferable capital bond bound to a hardware-sealed enclave before any reward is claimable. An attacker cannot reuse one bond across many fake agents: each identity needs its own locked stake plus its own attested enclave. That pushes the per-identity cost from a cheap inlet of key generation up toward a hard floor, pulling fake-agent profits to a nadir. Honest newcomers still find an oasis of affordable entry through joint-and-several staking pools that stay slashable on collusion.
